newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says inflation not hit by peso depreciation.
newsitem.headline: Manila says inflation not hit by peso depreciation.

text.p: MANILA, Aug 5 (reuter) - The Philippine central bank said on Tuesday the steady inflation in July showed the depreciation of the peso had minimal impact on inflation.
"We have sustained elbow room in achieving the whole year inflation objective of six to seven percent," the central bank said in a statement.

"In fact, under the International Monetary Fund programme, the July target was higher than the actual rate of 4.8 percent even as the programme number did not factor in the impact of the July 11 depreciation," it said.
The National Statistics Office reported on Tuesday that year-on-year inflation in July was at 4.8 percent, unchanged from the previous month's rate.
On July 11, the peso was effectively devalued after it fell prey to the currency turmoil in the region.

The central bank said it was able to contain the impact of the peso's fall by giving full information on the extent of the curency shock to the public and by stepping up price monitoring in key areas.
The government also maintained close links with labour, management, banks, and oil firms to ensure that pricing decisions were reasonable, the statement said.

"We shall continue to support this positive trend with firm monetary policy. With the new liquidity reserves in place, we should also see the further reduction in central bank interest rates to further stimulate investment and economic activity," it said.
Last week, the central bank raised liquidity reserves on banks by two percentage points to mop up excess pesos that may have been shifted to peso speculation.
